clue.text: One controls issue of notes after period of inflation

definitions.text: One controls issue of notes after period of inflation

parts.words: One controls issue of notes after period of inflation
parts.note: reads like a central banker printing banknotes after inflation, but describes a piper who blows up the bag and then lets the musical notes out

explanation.surface: A central banker regulates the printing of banknotes once prices have been soaring.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog notes the clue's 'One' points to the player, a piper, though the grid prints the instrument; the 'notes' are musical and the 'inflation' is filling the bag with air.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish wind instrument is a bag inflated by the player that feeds air to pipes sounding notes.

clue.text: By his confusion about love, revealing how immature youth is

indicators.note: about means around, so the muddled letters go round the zero
confusion signals that the letters of by his are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: His muddled thinking about love shows how young he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' turns BYHIS into BYISH; 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Youthfully immature behaviour is described as boyish, like that of a young lad.

clue.text: Great seriousness of cause producing mass movement

definitions.meaning: solemn weight of manner or of a situation
the physical force that pulls bodies with mass towards one another

explanation.surface: A grave cause that sets crowds marching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass movement' looks political, but it is physics: masses falling together.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both solemnity and the attractive force between masses.

clue.text: One represented Rome and Paris, as artistic director

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: represented read as re-presented means shown in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone acted for two capital cities as an arts manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges I, ROME and PARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and directs theatrical or musical productions.

clue.text: Self-centredness characteristic of Gregory?

definitions.meaning: the name Gregory has the word ego at its centre, so the name shows this quality

explanation.surface: A conceited man named Gregory is typically self-absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: GR-EGO-RY has EGO at its centre: 'ego-centricity'. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wrapped up in oneself, with the ego at the centre of everything, is selfishness.

clue.text: Stone put in ring, say, for rich people

parts.note: jet is a black gemstone
a stone put into a ring is set, as in a setting

explanation.surface: A gem is mounted in a ring for wealthy buyers.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are the wealthy, fashionable people who travel the world for pleasure.

clue.text: He led our race, once, in first place

definitions.meaning: Sir Anthony, Conservative prime minister from 1955 to 1957, once led the British nation
the Garden of Paradise in Genesis, the first home of humankind

explanation.surface: A runner who led our race once took first place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' is the nation (or mankind), not a running event.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Anthony bore the surname, and the biblical garden was humanity's first home.

clue.text: Spot polar explorer, say, one seen flying over ocean

indicators.note: say signals that the words are judged by how they are pronounced

parts.note: spot means see, and Richard Byrd was an American polar explorer

explanation.surface: Catch sight of the Antarctic adventurer, one seen flying over the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE BYRD sounds like SEA BIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull or albatross flying over the waves is a bird of the sea.

clue.text: Foolishly authorise scrapping old reference books

indicators.note: foolishly suggests the letters of authorise are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stupidly sanctions throwing out old dictionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrapping' removes O from AUTHORISE; 'Foolishly' then rearranges the remaining AUTHRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesauri, the plural of thesaurus, are books of synonyms used for reference.

clue.text: Dated agreement that ends on September 30?

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned word for yes, as in the ayes and the noes
a twelve-month stretch stopped at the end of September is only three quarters complete, so three of the word's four letters

explanation.surface: An old contract runs until the last day of September.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is playful: a year that stops at September 30 is three-quarters of a year, and three-quarters of YEAR is YEA. The question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic affirmative survives in parliamentary voting and old texts as an outdated yes.

clue.text: Favouring energy charge being spread

parts.note: pro means in favour of
life can mean vigour or energy, as in 'full of life'
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: Someone backs an energy tariff that is being rolled out widely.
explanation.definitionFit: To proliferate is to multiply and spread rapidly, a close synonym.

clue.text: Absurdly dressing mother like native, in a manner of speaking

definitions.text: like native, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: dressing means wrapping round, so the word for absurdly encloses the word for mother

parts.note: idiotically means stupidly or absurdly
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly clothes their mum in native garb, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absurdly' looks like an anagram signal but is a plain synonym, idiotically; 'dressing' is an image of clothing wrapped round mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking idiomatically means using expressions natural to a native speaker.

clue.text: Eccentric genius father backed, one of a kind

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of genius are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the word for father is read in reverse

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: An odd brilliant man was supported by his dad, a true original.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' turns GENIUS into SUIGEN; 'backed' turns SIRE into ERIS. SUI GENERIS is Latin for 'of its own kind'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase describes something unique, in a class all of its own.

clue.text: Prepare ship at a northern port

parts.note: to rig a ship is to fit it with masts, sails and ropes

explanation.surface: A sailor gets a vessel ready at a harbour in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga, capital of Latvia, is a Baltic seaport in northern Europe.

clue.text: Old-fashioned type found either part of Marxism- Leninism

definitions.text: Old-fashioned type found either part of Marxism- Leninism

parts.words: Old-fashioned type found either part of Marxism- Leninism
parts.note: reading Marxism backwards hides a figure inside it, and Leninism backwards hides another figure, so each half contains a reversed digit word

explanation.surface: Something out of date is found in each half of the old Soviet doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside MAR(XIS)M is SIX reversed and inside L(ENIN)ISM is NINE reversed: each part holds a number backwards. The phrase also means something dated.
explanation.definitionFit: A back number is an outdated person or thing, from an old issue of a magazine.

clue.text: Person dictating a couple of letters for typist with bombast

indicators.note: asks for just the opening pair of letters of the word typist

parts.note: a rant is a bombastic tirade

explanation.surface: A boss dictating to the typist does so with a lot of bluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of letters for' takes TY, the first two letters of 'typist'. 'Person dictating' looks like an office boss, but means a dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a despot, someone who rules as a dictator.

clue.text: Indirectly move us, as 'usband might put it

indicators.note: the dropped h shows the phrase is said in an h-less accent, so her becomes 'er

parts.note: us is me and her, as a husband might say of himself and his wife

explanation.surface: A Cockney husband speaks of shifting the two of them in a roundabout way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' for a husband is 'me and her'; dropping the H, as the clue's own ''usband' does, gives 'me an' 'er'.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander or wind about, moving along an indirect course.

clue.text: Part of shoe damaged sock

parts.note: the upper is the part of a shoe above the sole
cut means injured or damaged

explanation.surface: A piece of footwear has a torn sock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sock' looks like footwear; it is a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock is to punch, and an uppercut is an upward punch.

clue.text: Composer responsible for Toscanini's start

parts.note: seems to praise whoever launched the conductor's career, but the start of the word Toscanini is Tosca, the opera this Italian composer wrote

explanation.surface: A composer gave the great conductor Toscanini his big break.
explanation.walkthrough: Toscanini did premiere this composer's operas, which helps the misdirection; the real point is that the name Toscanini begins with the opera title Tosca.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian opera composer wrote Tosca, the first five letters of the conductor's surname.

clue.text: Sound contented, wrapped up in bed, spoilt

indicators.note: wrapped means surrounded, so the bed goes round the sound

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a cat sounds contented when it purrs

explanation.surface: A cosy purring sound from someone tucked up in bed who has been spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound contented' suggests a cat; 'up' reverses it because this is a down clue, and 'wrapped ... in' puts that inside the small bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt means rotten or tainted, so spoilt.

clue.text: Volunteers joining monarch it's infectious

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers mix with the ruler and catch something contagious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' as infectious is an old use, as in a taking disease.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of taking is catching or contagious, said of a disease.

clue.text: Something sweet, signifying love

definitions.meaning: a whispered endearment between lovers, sweet talk of no substance
Macbeth calls life a tale signifying zero, meaning of no value

explanation.surface: A sweet gesture, a token of love.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: sweet ___, the Macbeth line 'signifying ___', and love as a tennis score.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes 'sweet ___' and 'signifying ___', and love means zero.

clue.text: Allow in weapon? That's out of order

indicators.note: in places the word for allow within the weapon

parts.note: the Bren is a light machine gun
to OK something is to allow it

explanation.surface: Is letting a gun inside out of line?
explanation.definitionFit: Something broken is not working, out of order.

clue.text: Mark's replacement not ready for England yet

definitions.text: Mark's replacement not ready for England yet

parts.words: Mark's replacement not ready for England yet
parts.note: the German currency gave way to the shared money of most EU states, which Britain had not adopted when this was set

explanation.surface: A substitute for someone called Mark is not yet fit to play for England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a player's name; it is the Deutschmark.
explanation.definitionFit: The single European currency replaced the German mark, while Britain kept sterling.

clue.text: Such a person repeatedly, perhaps, introduces reductions

definitions.text: Such a person repeatedly, perhaps, introduces reductions

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word introduces may be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper keeps bringing in price cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' is the twist: both 'introduces' and 'reductions' rearrange to the answer, and the whole clue also describes the retailer, so it works as a semi-&lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person is a retailer who sells at reduced prices, which is exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: Half of our letters, a very small quantity

definitions.meaning: the first thirteen letters of the alphabet, its opening half
a tiny amount, a jot or particle

explanation.surface: Half the alphabet amounts to very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A to M' covers thirteen of the 26 letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest particle of an element stands for any tiny amount.

clue.text: Consider strike on railway that provides rural recreation

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: to count someone something is to consider them so
to club is to strike with a heavy stick

explanation.surface: Workers weigh up a rail stoppage on the line serving a rural leisure spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A country club is a sporting and social club in the countryside, offering golf and leisure.

clue.text: One learner in front of computer unit in class

indicators.note: these words put the learner piece before the next piece in the answer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the learner plate on a British car
K stands for a kilobyte, a unit of computer memory

explanation.surface: A single student sits at the front of the computer room in a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilk means kind or sort, as in 'people of that ilk', so a class.

clue.text: Floor-covering is so long one metre, about

parts.note: ta-ta and so long are both informal goodbyes

indicators.note: about signals turning back the two letters that follow

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rug is that long, about one metre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns I and M round to MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A tatami is a Japanese straw mat used as a floor covering.

clue.text: Kind of bomb that, shortly, may be dropped in part of London

definitions.text: Kind of bomb that, shortly, may be dropped in part of London

parts.words: Kind of bomb that, shortly, may be dropped in part of London
parts.note: the bomb abbreviated to H, and the letter H is dropped in Cockney London speech, as well as bombs being dropped on the city

explanation.surface: A type of bomb that could soon fall on a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' points to the H in H-bomb, and the East End habit of dropping aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: The H-bomb is the thermonuclear bomb named after this lightest gas, symbol H.
